firmwares.name: SLOOP
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.what: A live groovebox: tracks, layers, a step sequencer, song mode, punch-in effects and samples, played on the FM-1 in real time.

firmwares.name: JIANT FM
firmwares.author: juanjiant-bit
firmwares.what: A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings in thermal colours, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice…), mutating macros, song mode from SLOOP. Not yet tested much on a real FM-1.

firmwares.name: Skiff
firmwares.author: illuminus5
firmwares.what: Six tracks of synths and drums with a groovebox's workflow: fourteen engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions and locks, songs, PERFORM with scenes, six themes and a browser editor; FM6 sounds built from scratch on the unit. Built on Felucca, with most of Felucca 1.6.1's work brought over (the second core, MIDI LEARN, INSERT); Felucca's sounds and projects load. Also runs on the SMK-37 Pro. Coming from 1.x: 2.0 saves in new formats – update on Skiff's own page (it backs up and converts), or back up in its editor first.

firmwares.name: Felucca
firmwares.author: Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments)
firmwares.what: The custom firmware the others build on: the FM-1's own synth engines, a sequencer, effects and a better panel, with an editor in the browser.

firmwares.name: Melodee
firmwares.author: keremimo
firmwares.what: Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.
squeezed: nothing: the screen's send buffer moves to the firmware's .pool memory (RAM was short)

firmwares.name: Clipper
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.what: A deep synth grown out of SLOOP: 23 engines and 407 sounds, from HYBRID (three oscillators, two filters, a mod matrix) to six-operator FM, wavetables, wave sequencing, a Juno and physical models; arp, step sequencer, MPE and a web editor for every parameter.

firmwares.name: CoralFlower
firmwares.author: FicusFicusov
firmwares.what: Chords after the Orchid, with controls made for the FM-1: one key plays a chord with a bass note. Also 27 scales, an arpeggiator, a sequencer with drums and a song mode, and a pixel flower that grows as you play.

firmwares.name: GR!MM
firmwares.author: GR!MM
firmwares.what: Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream firmware: 4 tracks, 7 sound sources, real recorded choirs, tracks that play by themselves, and long tape, granular and reverb effects.

firmwares.name: GHOULBOX
firmwares.author: Jason Persinger
firmwares.what: Dungeon synth: a cathedral hall reverb, tape and crush, a hurdy-gurdy engine, choirs, organs and recorded psaltery and harp, an old-RPG screen with wall torches.

firmwares.name: DUB-1
firmwares.author: sbegueria
firmwares.what: A generative dub techno machine that plays itself from the moment it is on: chord stabs into a tape echo, FM pings, a sub bass on five grooves, a ducking kick, crackle, and an eight-bar arrangement with breaks and fills.

firmwares.name: Niagara Drift
firmwares.author: Evan Yerburgh
firmwares.what: A drone synth inspired by the SOMA Lyra-8, Moog Subharmonicon and Stylophone CPM DS-2. Two virtual-analog drones that breathe and drift on their own, with presets for instant ambient textures and full controls to push them into harsh, beating, self-oscillating sound.

firmwares.name: Fart Machine One
firmwares.author: adamcharleswilsonmusic-code
firmwares.what: A questionable musical instrument: ten artisanal farts, reverb, delay and a sixteen-step sequencer.

firmwares.name: SPAMPY
firmwares.author: Spampy-Droid
firmwares.what: SPAMPY 1.1: five-track synthwave FM-1 firmware with 170 synth presets, 44 drum kits including KAVINSKY, scenes, effects, 10 synthwave/atmospheric arpeggiators, extended envelope controls, corrected MIDI channel routing (no unintended synth or drum track triggering), dual-flash compatibility for…

firmwares.name: HYP-1
firmwares.author: RedtailWorks
firmwares.what: Hypnotic techno and acid: a breathing pad, a deep drone, a generative 303 line and grain over drums you sequence. Flip patterns on the bar, break it down, build it up. Forked from AMB-1. One of a pack of four: LOF-1 (a lofi groovebox), ECO-1 (a plant plays it) and GRAV-1 (a star and its planets), experimental, on its project page.

firmwares.name: NACHTFAHRT
firmwares.author: Cranky Man
firmwares.what: Generative 1970s Berlin School: two sequencers drift against each other over a drone, in eight endless pieces. Play a melody on the white keys and the lead answers it, takes it as its theme and grows new ideas from it.

firmwares.name: Rainbow Mode
firmwares.author: joshbartlettband-web
firmwares.what: A music toy for little children: 63 cartoon friends, every key in tune, chords, strumming, songs to follow and an ear game, notes on a staff, a volume cap for small ears.

firmwares.name: PERF-1
firmwares.author: deamonSLINKY
firmwares.what: A groovebox that plays itself while you steer it: 22 genres and 220 pieces that play like tracks, with builds, breakdowns and fills. Pad, bass, 303-style acid and DX7 pluck voices, 21 drum kits plus your own samples, an auto-DJ, effects on the keys and a web studio. Works on the newer FM-1s too.

firmwares.name: KARMA
firmwares.author: Ariel Muchnik
firmwares.what: A four-track groovebox: an acid bass or a Juno-style poly, physical modelling, two dozen synthesis models and a drum synth. A 64-step sequencer with song mode, generators that write parts on one chord plan, pixel characters, and USB audio with six stems, MIDI out and DAW sync.

firmwares.name: sloopDX
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: SLOOP's live workflow with Dexed's DX7 engine and 128 steps a track: six operators, 32 algorithms, your own .syx banks, every voice edited on the FM-1, FM drums you program.

firmwares.name: S1Vave
firmwares.author: Andrew GG
firmwares.what: An 8-voice virtual analog tweak synth: authentic 4-pole resonant filter, dual sub-oscillator, ADSR envelopes, 64-step sequencer, and hands-on live performance controls.

firmwares.name: CHOPPAH
firmwares.author: Laurens Profittlich
firmwares.what: An Amen break chopper for the FM-1: eight classic breaks cut into 16 slices on the white keys, hold a key to loop it. Black keys are momentary pads for rolls, reverse, freeze, tape stop, gate, filter and dub throws. A generator rearranges the break live, with a four-slot FX chain and a DJ filter.
firmwares.via: Charles Vestal's fm1-base mirror, turned on

firmwares.name: fm1-dock
firmwares.author: Joakim Eriksson
firmwares.what: One firmware, many synths: hold HOME and pick CS-1, Scintilla (the Elka Synthex), OberVave or a sine, no reflashing. Add PROPHET, B3 ORGAN, Niagara Drift, ARTIHIVE, FM-106, FM-1 SID, AMB-1, FoMni, MONK-1, FiMba-1, GATOR, DUB-1, FMINI-1, FM6, ATEK303 or KEYS from the page with one click, and your…

firmwares.name: zp12
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: A 12-bit sampler after the E-mu SP-1200: sample on the FM-1 itself (a computer or phone plays into it over USB) or in the browser (mic, line-in or a file), and it plays on its own. Gritty and unsmoothed, with loops and songs.

firmwares.name: DARK-1
firmwares.author: Polystellarflow
firmwares.what: Dark-music firmware for the FM-1: 21 genres, 210 pieces, dark techno to dark ambient and darkwave. Wander evolves it on its own. Arp, Dice, step editor, new visuals, simpler settings, bigger text. Works on older and newer FM-1s (both flash chips).

firmwares.name: CS-1
firmwares.author: twochannels
firmwares.what: A Yamaha CS-80 in spirit: eight voices of two channels, high- and low-pass filters in series, ring modulator, the touch response and 22 tones from the owner's manual. A sound module played over MIDI.

firmwares.name: FiMba-1
firmwares.author: jadamsowers
firmwares.what: A physically modelled kalimba: tines laid out like the real one, thumb-roll chords, mbira patterns, a sound hole to cover, grains, tape and a plate reverb. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: K-WASUB
firmwares.author: Omnipotard (Guizmoh)
firmwares.what: Runs on the latest FM-1 chip. A bass synth for DnB, dubstep, dub and techno: deep subs, reese, growls and 808s. Two of nine engines play together, the keys change the wobble live, and one button plus a knob puts an LFO on any setting. With drums, a bass sequencer and live FX pads.

firmwares.name: FMEL-1
firmwares.author: Antonio Altea
firmwares.what: Mellotron-style tape sounds, coloured with effects and lo-fi tape: flutes, strings and choirs as on the old tape frames, played from the keys.

firmwares.name: Guru-600
firmwares.author: Marc Massé
firmwares.what: The FM-1 becomes a Prophet-600: 255 sounds (the 100 factory programs, 100 from the free 2022 collection, 55 of its own), a web editor in 7 languages with a panel inspired by the Prophet-600, four tracks with sequencer, arpeggiator, morph and two insert effects each. Based on Felucca.

firmwares.name: Golana
firmwares.author: Gadlele
firmwares.what: One analog-style synth laid out like the classic microKORG, with a screen that draws the sound.

firmwares.name: h1
firmwares.author: Jake Handy
firmwares.what: handy-1 (h1): sixteen instruments, each a full-screen animated picture you play. PRESETS changes the instrument, ALGORITHM changes its character, and the four knobs always shape the sound and the picture together. Loop recorder, step sequencer, arpeggiator and metronome built in.
firmwares.via: Charles Vestal's fm1-base mirror, turned on

firmwares.name: ORBIT
firmwares.author: dspaudio
firmwares.what: A four-track groovebox: three synths and a drum machine in a colour-coded Synth, Drum, Event Tape and Mixer workflow, loops turned into songs, user macros, screens after the OP-1. Based on SLOOP.

firmwares.name: FuMi-1
firmwares.author: cartesive
firmwares.what: A shigin conductor after the Suiko ST-50: its two rows of keys, the key set in honsū, equal or its own just tuning, a koto and twelve more sounds on a 6-op FM engine, ring time, vibrato, trill and a looper.

firmwares.name: fm1-chord
firmwares.author: math0ne
firmwares.what: A chord machine after the HiChord, with extras: chords in a key under the white keys, slash chords and inversions, sounds, envelopes, effects and a looper.

firmwares.name: Penumbra
firmwares.author: Lunar Eclipse Forge
firmwares.what: An ambient space-drone synth that plays itself until you do. Drone voices drift in and out, a far-off voice sings, and the sound glides from scene to scene as an eclipse crosses the screen. Every key is in tune, and loops follow each key change. A thick, slow drone, like the Solar 42.

firmwares.name: Chipbox
firmwares.author: pbarilla
firmwares.what: A ultra-refined Chiptune music editor, featuring over 35 classic chips such as NES, Gameboy, heck even the Sunsoft 5B! Pages with their own meter, tempo and glide, so waltzes and 7/8 grooves are easy. Gimmick fans rejoice!

firmwares.name: Frodhes
firmwares.author: Leonardo Mirabal
firmwares.what: An electric piano, vibraphone and marimba, physically modelled, no samples, with drive, tremolo or wah, phaser, chorus, delay and reverb (hall, plate, infinite), tap tempo and MIDI clock sync, an arpeggiator, a sequencer, scales and presets.

firmwares.name: AISLING
firmwares.author: CU_STE
firmwares.what: Irish ambient music that plays itself for ever: harps, flute and drone. Eight pieces to steer, or play along on its keys, a keyboard or a DAW. Now an app on your iPhone too, no FM-1 needed. Its visualiser paints the music as an Irish landscape.

firmwares.name: Mini-Tone
firmwares.author: Stéphane Schmitz
firmwares.what: Felucca with six tracks and new engines: SID, Braids' 48 models, a TB-303 and engines after Elektron's Analog Four, SY Chip and Digitone 2, a ping-pong delay and a new reverb. Built on Felucca 1.5.

firmwares.name: MAKU
firmwares.author: okumurari
firmwares.what: An ambience machine for DJ interludes: switch it on and a random world in key plays, four parts, buttons that are verbs, and the worlds you like breed new ones. Clock follow. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: Blop
firmwares.author: Obsimo
firmwares.what: Explore sound with your Blop: one-finger chords from 38 grids, chord rhythms, a bass with its own riffs and a few discreet drums with sidechain, while a little creature swims to your chords in an aquarium on the screen. Chords and bass go out as MIDI over USB.
firmwares.via: Charles Vestal's fm1-base mirror, turned on

firmwares.name: NOIZ DEMONS
firmwares.author: SPIKE the Percussionist
firmwares.what: Felucca with randomization as a ritual: every new sound summons one of 30 demons of the Ars Goetia, its sigil takes the screen and its rank decides how wild the sound gets.

firmwares.name: KAWA
firmwares.author: Omnipotard
firmwares.what: A pocket tracker for chiptune and IDM: six tracks of pulse, 4-bit wave, noise, 6-operator FM, drum kits and samples. Chain patterns into songs, chop breaks, and play 64 live effects (with K-GLITCH's DESTROY and BEAT), a filter and an FX sequencer.

firmwares.name: WaveLoop FM-1
firmwares.author: ELI7VH
firmwares.what: Felucca played from an Arturia MiniLab 3: track faders, a DJ filter, momentary effect pads; 32 patches a bank, 12 evolving songs, revoiced 808 and CR78 kits.

firmwares.name: HADAL-1
firmwares.author: Polystellarflow
firmwares.what: Generative dark ambient: drones, demonic and angelic choirs, bells and 135 sound effects that keep changing by themselves across 15 worlds, with 40 melting pictures. Play bells or latch choir voices on the keys, or play and hold effects. Works on older and newer FM-1s (both flash chips).
firmwares.via: Charles Vestal's fm1-base mirror, turned on

firmwares.name: SLOOP DX7 Banks
firmwares.author: majnikool
firmwares.what: SLOOP 2.4 with up to twelve DX7 voice banks, kept and named in the editor, presets by kind. Test builds: back up first.

firmwares.name: Smileyface
firmwares.author: pbarilla
firmwares.what: You're making acid, baby! Smash that LFO button until you hear something you like, and then twist those knobs! Now with 100% more FX! A truly trippy experience! Built on Chipbox.

firmwares.name: sloop-DUB
firmwares.author: altessproduction
firmwares.what: a four-band isolator with mute bands, a bipolar DJ filter, per-track echo throws, a tape echo and a siren voice. The bank: 180 genre presets, 38 kits and all 75 riddims of the Riddim Collection grid (African Beat, Real Rock, Sleng Teng), each loading its four patterns: bass, skank, the rest, drums.

firmwares.name: PurpleMonkey
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.what: A first instrument for toddlers: random key bashing and knob turning are rewarded with dancing animated pets and little musical sequences. Press a key, any key.

firmwares.name: Tuna
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.what: Generative music for the FM-1: it composes as it plays, melody, bass, accompaniment and percussion shaped by music theory out of controlled randomness. Pick a composer or one of 86 genres across eight decades and it plays in that manner, endlessly and never twice the same.

firmwares.name: DRIFT
firmwares.author: FBNFRTG
firmwares.what: An ambient instrument for live sessions: warm synths, spacious pads and delicate plucks over a generative Euclidean sequencer on one track, with delays and reverbs from spring to shimmer. Built on Felucca.

firmwares.name: ARTIHIVE
firmwares.author: KHAV
firmwares.what: Eight-voice experimental drone and polyphonic FM synthesizer with four interacting pairs, envelopes, legato glide, hyper LFO, stereo motion, dual modulated delay and a 1-16 step arpeggiator and sequencer. Artistically inspired by SOMA LYRA-8; independently developed.

firmwares.name: Arcturus S6
firmwares.author: Zeptosecond DSP
firmwares.what: An experimental, self-playing wavetable instrument for generative, evolving soundscapes. Four PPG-style oscillators, Serge-style function generators, sample-and-holds and logic, patched through mod and gate matrices. 12 bit, 22kHz, green phosphor CRT, Fairlight-style pages.

firmwares.name: SATIE-1
firmwares.author: OCKM Studio
firmwares.what: Erik. Evolved. Ten Satie pieces become an evolving electronic soundtrack in five moods. Choose a tune, set the pace and blend Solo, Duet or Trio. Shape each instrument, add vinyl colour and synced delay, or simply let it play. GLO opens the quick guide.

firmwares.name: FM1 Quest
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.what: A pixel-art RPG while you make music, built on SLOOP: four heroes, one a track, walk through a village and fight monsters and bosses as your loop plays, every SLOOP screen redrawn in the game's style.

firmwares.name: Pocket GammaWave
firmwares.author: ShadowTune (GammaWave Audio)
firmwares.what: The companion to the GammaWave desktop synth: four industrial distortions, vowel and scream filters, an FFT spectrogram, a four-track tape deck screen and a song generator with 49 genres, trap and drill too.

firmwares.name: J6
firmwares.author: JackieAlacrity2373
firmwares.what: A six-voice JUNO-60 style polysynth with chorus, arpeggiator and a 16-step recorder. 56 factory sounds, a MIDI control for every knob, and a free browser editor that plays it over USB-MIDI.
firmwares.via: Charles Vestal's fm1-base mirror, turned on

firmwares.name: Scintilla
firmwares.author: Joakim Eriksson
firmwares.what: The 1981 Elka Synthex on the FM-1: all 80 factory sounds, Paul Wiffen's laser harp among them, checked sample by sample against the original. Two layers of 8 voices (single, split, double), poly, mono or unison, chorus and reverb, and the four knobs edit what is on the screen.

firmwares.name: Del Rio
firmwares.author: Jess Del Rio
firmwares.what: A rhythm box of ceremony percussion: djembe, cajon, udu, clapsticks, maracas and triangle on the black keys, a step sequencer on the white keys. The berimbau and the capoeira's bateria have their own page. A tanpura and a shruti box sound alone or under the rhythm.
firmwares.via: Charles Vestal's fm1-base mirror, turned on

firmwares.name: SLOOP Floyd FM
firmwares.author: René Bohne
firmwares.what: SLOOP with a visual four-operator FM engine after Floyd Steinberg's 4-OP idea: an ADSR per operator, seven pages, a live oscilloscope that draws the envelopes as you play.

firmwares.name: Jangada
firmwares.author: zednaked
firmwares.what: Dark, industrial, Brazilian: drones that breathe, ten engines (6-op FM, a superwave analog with a ladder filter), four tracks, a mod matrix, live effects.

firmwares.name: MIN-1
firmwares.author: Reytian
firmwares.what: A tiny minimalist ensemble after Philip Glass: it starts playing when you switch on, you join whenever you like. In EASY mode every white key is a chord that fits. Four models, twenty pieces.

firmwares.name: Drumlab
firmwares.author: pbarilla
firmwares.what: Microtonic, for the FM-1! Roll the dice for a kit, build one from scratch, or bring in your Microtonic presets and patterns. Share kits and patterns as files, and send it all to your Teenage Engineering PO-32! Built on Chipbox!

firmwares.name: FM1-GM
firmwares.author: jartificer
firmwares.what: A General MIDI sequencer with 16 tracks, 128 General MIDI instruments to choose from and a drum kit (on track 10). It can store up to 64 songs, each containing up to 128 measures.

firmwares.name: Vector37
firmwares.author: genkigenki
firmwares.what: An orbiting overtone synth: four corners of two overtone generators each, a sun on a path and a moon around it decide how much of each you hear; the knobs shape the selected planet. Made for the SMK-37, here its FM-1 build. After the Beetlecrab Vector.

firmwares.name: Cut-A-Dor
firmwares.author: Kid Bunka
firmwares.what: A beat dojo for scratch DJs and beatmakers: boom bap, lo-fi and breaks from 16 rhythm families with swing and fills, an eight-lane 32-step sequencer, punch-in effects you record bar by bar, a bass voice. Sound banks and editor in the browser.

firmwares.name: Felucca [Salt]
firmwares.author: Chance Roth (ChanceTheMaker)
firmwares.what: Felucca with a hardware-inspired Studio in the browser (play it there without an FM-1): many engines, presets, skins. A beta.

firmwares.name: Felucca 8 Patterns
firmwares.author: echoe
firmwares.what: An LLM-written expansion of Felucca with eight patterns per track, pattern chaining (up to 512 steps/pattern), per-step patch switching, multiple new chord modes, generative arpeggiator, new synth engines LEAD and SH-DRUM, borrowed engines SWARM, FM-TONE, and WAVETONE from Mini-Tone, new effects…

firmwares.name: MODELAR
firmwares.author: Hirakos
firmwares.what: A semi-modular drone synth played like a Kaoss Pad: four oscillators modulating each other through eight routings, and keys that move a cursor on an XY pad instead of playing notes: white keys are points, black keys gestures. ARP, a polymetric sequencer, a clock in Hz and eight generative environments.
firmwares.via: Charles Vestal's fm1-base mirror, turned on

firmwares.name: OPN-1
firmwares.author: putchdev
firmwares.what: The Sega Genesis / Mega Drive's Yamaha YM2612: six channels of 4-operator FM. Its web app takes patches from game music (VGM) and OPM files and streams VGM tunes to the FM-1 to play.

firmwares.name: HERA
firmwares.author: Ben Badio
firmwares.what: A chord groovebox after the Roland J-6: 100 chord sets, 9 phrase styles with 12 variations each and a 64-pattern step sequencer, on a four-voice Juno-style synth from Clipper with chorus, delay and reverb. A chord map on the screen shows which chord sits on which key. Built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: NEON
firmwares.author: Neon Summers
firmwares.what: A synthwave groovebox: Juno pads, supersaw leads, pulsing basses and 80s drum machines. Pick a mood and one chord progression drives every track; WRITE drafts a part for each sound and VARY turns a bar into a 4-bar phrase. About 220 presets sorted by role.

firmwares.name: ANDROMEDA
firmwares.author: Polaris Sound Lab
firmwares.what: Ambient music that writes itself. Choose one of 13 moods and ALIGN builds a whole 4-track piece, always in key; AUTO keeps it growing from your own notes. A three-head SPACE TAPE echo with spring, SKY macros, and visions drawn live from the sound: cymatics, harmonograph, attractor and orrery.

firmwares.name: SID-1
firmwares.author: putchdev
firmwares.what: The Commodore 64's SID chip, twice for six voices. Its web app edits patches and takes them straight from .sid game music files.

firmwares.name: Bytemania
firmwares.author: lloyd (llozd)
firmwares.what: A bytebeat synth: play one-line formulas, tweak them with the knobs, and write your own, with a random button in the formula creator that is really fun. A beta, built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: ZENITH-1
firmwares.author: Polystellarflow
firmwares.what: Generative ambient that plays itself, and you can steer it: swap the sounds of the pads, bells, bass, beats, lead and air, guide where it goes, or let it wander through 8 worlds. 27 melodic effects, strum or play the lead on the keys. Works on older and newer FM-1s.
firmwares.via: Charles Vestal's fm1-base mirror, turned on

firmwares.name: B3 ORGAN
firmwares.author: R-Jeb
firmwares.what: A B3 tonewheel organ computed from setBfree's own data: 91 wheels, drawbars for three manuals, key click, vibrato and chorus, percussion, overdrive, reverb, a Leslie and an output equalizer. All 110 setBfree programs, 16 of your own, and a web editor that reads and stores the FM-1's sound.

firmwares.name: Ombak
firmwares.author: Lunar Eclipse Forge
firmwares.what: A shimmering bronze ensemble from Bali and Java that plays itself the moment you switch on. Touch a white key and gongs, drums and interlocking bells follow your melody; rest and it carries on. Eleven measured tunings, lively to meditative, and a sound-module mode for your DAW.

firmwares.name: STRANGER SYNTH
firmwares.author: swtdr34mz
firmwares.what: A performance synth in the spirit of the 80s analogue film scores: walls of detuned saws, arps on either hand following MIDI clock, chords from one finger, a sidechain, a heartbeat as the groove, eight tape and VHS performance effects, LINK to a second FM-1 with SIX MACHINES. A small town at night…
firmwares.via: Charles Vestal's fm1-base mirror, turned on

firmwares.name: glitch
firmwares.author: saulofilho
firmwares.what: Neon-noir groovebox firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1: four tracks, seven sources, tape and megacity space FX, sixteen scales (Insen, Hirajoshi, Iwato, whole tone), and forty-four Blade Runner factory sounds. Its screen: a glitched landscape that tears with the sound.

firmwares.name: Loom FM-1
firmwares.author: Co-oscillator
firmwares.what: Four synth and sampler tracks and a drum track on 14 engines, among them wavetable, 6-op FM, tape scrub, granular and a slicer; a 64-step sequencer, a chord progression generator, macros and sidechain ducking.

firmwares.name: DABKE
firmwares.author: STUDIOMORPHIK
firmwares.what: An Arabic wedding keyboard. Maqam scales with quarter tones on any note, dabke and shaabi rhythms, mijwiz, zurna, oud and qanun voices, a drone, eight tracks with loops and steps. Lean on a key and the note bends. An Akai MIDImix works as its mixer.
firmwares.via: Charles Vestal's fm1-base mirror, turned on

firmwares.name: Trumpagotchi
firmwares.author: Trust This Mechanism
firmwares.what: An unofficial parody virtual pet with a playable pentatonic keyboard. Feed, praise, clean up after and rest the pet. When he's happy, he joins your playing on bongos.

firmwares.name: VIBE FM Link
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: Play the VIBE FM VST plugin with your FM-1. Install this and the FM-1 is the controller: the keys play, KNOB 1-4 and every button do in the plugin what they do on the FM-1 – SLOOP, Felucca, OberVave and the other converted firmwares feel like home, in your DAW, in the Web Player and on the VIBE FM. The sound comes from the plugin, not the FM-1. Plain MIDI: any synth or DAW can learn it too.

firmwares.name: Daurade
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.what: Grooves in chrome: filtered, pumping, robotic. Press PLAY and Daurade plays a filtered loop that opens over sixteen bars, a mix that pumps on every kick, a robot voice singing the hook and crisp drums. Ten styles; steer it with four knobs, drop it, set off a solo or play the lead yourself.

firmwares.name: AETHER FM1
firmwares.author: GR!MM
firmwares.what: Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream firmware: 4 tracks, 7 sound sources, real recorded choirs, tracks that play by themselves, and long tape, granular and reverb effects.
